description.narrative: Bidragen syftar till att skapa en inkluderande informationsmiljö för att förbättra medborgarnas tillgång till oberoende information av hög kvalitet som gör det möjligt för dem att delta i landets övergång till demokrati och ställa sina nya ledare till svars.

The contribution aims at creating an inclusive information environment to improve citizens’ access to high quality independent information that enables them to participate in the country’s democratic transition and hold their new leaders to account

Overall Objective: - Contribute to peace building, security and social cohesion in Sudan.
Project Objective: - Create a conducive environment to improve citizens access to high-quality information that enables them to make better-informed decisions, foster social cohesion and holds power to account.
Intermediate objective 1: - Build the capacity of (media outlets, Journalists, citizen journalists) to cover political processes professionally and securely.
Intermediate objective 2: - Support CSOs and strengthen collaboration between the media and other civil society actors.
Intermediate objective 3: - Reinforce the operational resilience of media and information providers through rapid response support

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
A Media Mapping Assessment was Conducted by the EMA project in February 2023, accurately predicted the affiliations of media outlets. The research extensively answered the question; What are the different typologies of media initiatives which exist in Sudan today? How and why did they emerge and how will they sustain themselves? The report informed operational and technical planning, and was shared with donor and media development organizations. The mapping Informed the EMA project selection of local partners for future projects.
A Region Specific Audience Assessment was conducted by Thomson Foundation that showed various consumption patterns across Sudan and media literacy through answering the question How and why Sudanese Audience are accessing media and what is their view of its content? Two partners appeared in the research on audience and media consumption habits conducted by TF in November 2022. Overall, it resulted in showing the importance of local news to build trust with the audience and relevance of media content to the audience.
Core Sub-granting Mechanism to six Media Outlets supported financial sustainability subgrants mainly for marginalized, youth led media outlets. Partner specific impact includes: Established an office/ studio in Kampala, content from SPLMN controlled areas to Sudanese in other locations. Produced series of podcasts (by love, middle ground, you got the mic, Sudan untold stories), each episode has a reach of at least 200k.
Media for Peace Grant achieved the following: Music residency: A 9-day musical residency gathering 8 musicians from Darfur, the Nuba Mountains, Sinnar, Bejrawia, and Khartoum. The residency was held June 9-20th in Kampala, UG. A total of 8 musicians, 4 males and 4 females representing the Masalit, Fur, Nyala, Sinnar, Bejrawia, and Nuba Mountains. The residency was an incubation program for displaced Sudanese musicians and refugees, grounding them in their new environment through collaborative relationships, and expanding their network and musical knowledge. Eighteen songs were presented at the end of the residency on the second day of Festival Al-Shaab to a crowd of more than 100 people. Languages represented were Khartoum Arabic, Fur, Masalit, Darfur Arabic, and Toro
Festival Al-Shaab, a 3-day festival held in Kampala, resulting in the participation of more than 125 Sudanese activists, artists and media professionals. The festival included various sessions on monitoring and documentation of human rights violations, international justice mechanisms such as ICC, music production, documentary making masterclass, mobile cinema masterclass. It also resulted in providing a space for Sudanese artists, journalists and activists to network with Ugandan media and art hubs.
Internews Global Technology Hub (GTH) developed two websites and provided helpdesk support to the 6 partners, with a total number of 34 tickets responded to. Supported digital security requests by journalists such by providing 7 VPNs and securing journalists mobile phones while they relocated following the outbreak of the war. These actions resulted in helping partner journalists to avoid security issues at checkpoints, where it is common for phones to be searched.
44 (14 Female/ 30 Male) journalists participated in the biweekly editorial training sessions and followed by mentorship. Training and mentorship topics varied from general editorial support, editing basics, journalism ethics, 5Ws, interviewing survivors of violence, to sources and data visualization.
A 5-day workshop conducted in Nairobi with the participation of 39 journalists (17F/22M) coming from exile, SPLMN controlled areas and SLA-Abdul-Wahid areas. Topics covered include conflict sensitive reporting, conflict analysis, ethics, research and open-source investigation, multimedia production and tackling hate speech.
Support to 30 women media professionals and civil society organisation (CSO) actors in exile through a She Speaks project which is a 6-week mentoring and support program focused on storytelling and advocacy, psychosocial support and digital security.
Designed WhatsApp course for Digital Training on Addressing SGBV during Conflict with 5 modules training on SGBV. 64 people completed the training in English of which 35 received certificates.
Through EMAs Rapid Response Grants mechanism, the project supported 104 journalists with relocation grants
A psychosocial support expert held 62 group sessions for a total of 50 journalists and 833 individual sessions with 74 journalists (43 Male, 31 Female). Survey conducted in March 2024 show: 100% of participants found sessions to be helpful. 100% of respondents affirmed that the sessions played a role in fulfilling their work responsibilities effectively. All respondents agreed that psychosocial health care is an essential element in their work to maintain productivity. All recipients said that they had or would recommend the psychosocial support sessions to others.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
